title: Column cohomology of the specified Cech resolution double complex
statement: Let C be a category with v-small Hom sets and finite wide pullbacks, J a Grothendieck topology with sheafification for v-small abelian groups, F an abelian sheaf, I an injective resolution of F [def-sp-injective-resolutions], X an object of C, and pi_i : U_i → X a family indexed by a type in universe v. Assume that Ext in the category of abelian sheaves can be computed in universe v. For every q ≥ 0, taking inner-degree q cohomology of D [def-sc-cech-resolution-double-complex] gives a complex naturally isomorphic to the Cech complex of the presheaf V ↦ H^q(V,F) [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with the horizontal differential equal to the Cech differential. No covering hypothesis is required.

source.place: Step 2: identify vertical cohomology and its horizontal differential; lem-sc-cech-spectral Step 1.

proof.text: The free abelian sheaf on the representable of V represents evaluation at V, by the sheafification and free abelian Yoneda adjunctions. Thus Ext computed with I identifies H^q(I(V)) with H^q(V,F), naturally in V.

For each p, the vertical complex of D is a product of these evaluation complexes. Kernels and images of products of maps of abelian groups are computed componentwise (choose preimages for each component), so its cohomology is the product of their cohomologies.

The evaluation comparison is natural for projections of fibre products. Consequently it commutes with every coface map, hence with their alternating sum. Assemble the degreewise isomorphisms into the asserted complex isomorphism.

theorem Sheaf.cechResolutionDoubleComplex_columns
    {F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v}} (I : InjectiveResolution F) (X : C)
    {ι : Type v} {U : ι → C} (π : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X) (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor _ (ComplexShape.up ℕ) q).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (Sheaf.cechResolutionDoubleComplex I X π) ≅
      (cechComplexFunctor fun i ↦ Over.mk (π i)).obj
        ((Over.forget X).op ⋙ F.cohomologyPresheaf q))
